blurb.workdog.hunting_group: %s is a hunting dog. If you put %6$s in working mode, %5$s will target an entity that you attack. %2$s will get Looting on any kill, so tell %6$s what to do and let %6$s do the hard work for you!
blurb.workdog.bay_group: %s is a baying dog. WORK IN PROGRESS
blurb.workdog.terrier_group: %s is a tenacious terrier dog. %2$s lives to track down and torment pests, and in working mode, %5$s will use %7$s fast feet and ferocious teeth to track down and attack anything you target.
blurb.workdog.guardian_group: %s is a loving livestock guardian dog. If you put %6$s to work, %5$s won’t follow you, but will stay close to other passive entities. When a threat gets too close, %5$s will warn it away, and punish predators - and players - that don’t listen.
blurb.workdog.herding_group: %s is a humble herding dog. If you put %6$s in working mode, %5$s will be able to move livestock animals. %2$s can move huge groups all at once - guide %6$s where to go, and your animals will follow!
blurb.workdog.sled_group: %s is a sled dog. In working mode, hook %6$s up to a sled or cart, and let ‘em go! Sled dogs love to run, and love to work with other dogs, and %5$s will get where %5$s’s going even faster with friends.
blurb.workdog.protection_group: %s is a proud protection dog. In working mode, %5$s will follow you and warn away hostiles that come too close. If the bark doesn’t work, the bite will start, and %5$s will punish anything that breaches your personal bubble.
blurb.workdog.retriever_group: %s is a retriever dog. In working mode, %5$s will seek out dropped items, arrows and tridents, pick them up, and hold them in %7$s inventory for you. Give %6$s a saddle bag for more potential!
blurb.workdog.toy_group: %s is a toy dog. While %5$s can’t actually work, %5$s can do an even more important job: keeping you company. Or, that’s what you tell yourself. %2$s isn’t exactly paying rent, now, is %5$s?
blurb.workdog.support_group: %s is a support dog. In work mode, %5$s will follow you and provide support: whether it’s sniffing out treasure, digging up goodies, or giving you a stat boost, you don’t have to give %6$s much direction!
blurb.workdog.wolf:
Wolves are large, social carnivorous canines, native to several places with cold, arid grasslands to grow the large herbivore prey they need. Wolves’ natural social nature helped them become our closest companions.

Wild wolves don’t follow a militaristic “alpha-omega” structure. Instead, a pair of wolves will sleep, hunt, eat and travel with their offspring, and sometimes siblings or a vagrant from another pack. They have dozens of unique sounds and body language cues, and hunt and raise pups cooperatively.

Wolves have been killed as livestock predators for centuries, and still are. They are also threatened by the spread of diseases, like rabies and distemper, from feral dogs. Wolves are generally no threat to humans, but do pursue livestock as prey as other options become scarce. Using livestock guardian dogs can scare wolves away, and help us coexist peacefully.
blurb.workdog.akita:
Calculating and challenging, this giant Spitz breed doesn’t bark… but it definitely bites. This quiet, reserved dog is known for its immense loyalty, its bear-like bulk, and a dubious honor of devastating, unpredictable attacks. Bred for centuries to grab game by the horns, wrestle down fighting dogs, and ward off strangers, the akita doesn’t suffer fools.

Precarious politics, war and disease make this breed’s history complicated. Originally of Japanese origin, the original matagi akita is long gone. The American akita has been developed using military working breeds for a bull-headed but biddable dog. Contrarily, the Inu type is bred to a more symbolic standard, and a more delicate personality. They are increasingly considered separate breeds.

Many things can go wrong with an akita, and finding a good breeder is mandatory. Stubborn, aloof akitas rarely show what they’re feeling, and can be hard to read and harder to train with a gentle hand. However, when everything goes right, the earnest respect of an akita is truly something special.
blurb.workdog.border_collie:
Brainy border collies come from Scotland, and need their famous smarts to listen and respond to commands from a handler to move sheep. Energetic, playful and smart to a fault, these dogs need a job to do and a person to give them one, or they can quickly get anxious and destructive. Borders are eager, fast learners, and can do nearly any job an owner gives them.

Because border collies are bred for their working chops and not their coats, they can have a lot of different features. Tall ears, floppy ears, differently colored eyes, and even long or short coats are fair game, as long as the dogs can do their job. Peppy personalities, quick responses and good health are truly what border breeders want.

Collie owners should carefully consider the needs of their companion. Borders need lots of mental and physical stimulation to stay happy and healthy. They belong on a farm or with an active owner, who’s willing to give them a job to do and the respect they need.
blurb.workdog.boston_terrier:
A pugnacious, playful pup, this terrier is sometimes known as the “American gentleman.” Easy to train, easy to groom, and small enough for an apartment or townhome, these dogs are great family pets. Fitting for their formal flair, these little dogs are quite the socialites, and tend to mingle well with visitors and other pets.

Unfortunately, their extreme features mean these strong spirits struggle. Short-faced dogs like Bostons have health problems that shorten their lives, and make their later years painful. While not as bad as the similar-looking frenchies, they can have lots of eye, ear, nose and throat issues, overheat easily, and mother dogs can struggle to give birth safely.

Prospective Boston owners should only support breeders who test for health issues and have a long record of long-lived, healthy dogs. Longer snouts can actually be a sign of bad, off-standard breeding, and good airways are what really matters. If no breeders fit that bill, it’s best to look at other breeds.
blurb.workdog.german_shepherd:
Iconic and unmistakable, this pastoral pup needs no introduction. German shepherds were bred in the Alsatian region to herd and protect livestock, but they have the brains and brawn to do a lot of other jobs. Smart and active, and very protective, they can either be wonderful, well-socialized dogs or aggressive, dangerous disasters. Ultimately, it all starts with their breeding.

German shepherds are adaptable. Because they can play lots of parts, they have been bred into lots of different lines for police work, military work, search and rescue, as we ll as show and pet homes. Unfortunately, after decades of extreme breeding, all of them have some serious drawbacks.

Pet and show German shepherds are infamous for hip and spine issues from extreme breeding, while working line shepherds can be so anxious they are impossible to handle. Sadly, their anxiety often becomes aggression, and they end up in shelters to be euthanized. Owners should carefully consider all of these factors, and may want to consider other breeds with the traits they desire.
blurb.workdog.jack_russell_terrier:
Jack russells are an iconic companion to heroes in media, and a vicious hero in the battle against vermin. Bred to hunt foxes, now mostly used in pest control and as family pets, the Jack is a tenacious terrier with lots of energy.

Despite being a popular pet, Jacks can be dangerous and destructive. They’re working dogs through and through, and are notorious for playing rough and biting children, and for killing other pets. A bored Jack will dig out of a fenced yard, or chew through a wall to find something more interesting to do. They require an active owner, and aren’t always the best with kids.

To be up to standard, jacks need to be fearless, vocal and super smart, able to solve problems and stare death in the face. If you’re a farmer with property and a rat problem, Jacks are a great breed - if not, you might want to look at others that don’t harbor the hateful soul of a larger, more ferocious dog.
blurb.workdog.pit_bull:
It can’t be denied: this group of “misunderstood” breeds are the cause of most human injuries and fatalities. High prey drives, unpredictable body language and a devastating bite means that these dogs are ticking time bombs without proper management.

Bully-type dogs were bred to fight and kill bulls for entertainment, and when that was outlawed, they were turned against other dogs and bred to fight to the death. Even with a service dog vest and cute tutu, it’s impossible to undo their heritage, and they are still strong dogs with a penchant for aggression. Their horrible history, however, can be turned into awesome working potential by the right owners, and they are fantastic in extreme sports and at hog hunting.

Owners should be ready to control a 90-lb dog, and only buy from breeders who prefer steady temperaments to bow legs and blue merle coats. It’s tough to say no to rescues with rough pasts, but they’re a big ask for owners who may not get their full story. If you must bring home a bully, do it responsibly.
